title: Finite exactness of internal scalar restriction without closedness
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a monoidal category with finite limits and finite colimits ([def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]). Let $R,S$ be monoid objects of $\mathcal C$ and $\varphi:R\to S$ a morphism of monoid objects ([sk-def-sfb-ring-object]). Suppose that $R\otimes-$ and $S\otimes-$ preserve finite colimits. Then the internal module categories $\Mod_R(\mathcal C)$ and $\Mod_S(\mathcal C)$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]) have finite limits and finite colimits, and restriction of scalars
$$
\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}:\Mod_S(\mathcal C)\longrightarrow\Mod_R(\mathcal C)
$$
([def-sfb-modobj-restriction]) preserves finite limits and finite colimits, hence is exact ([def-galois-exact-functor]). No braiding, closed structure, commutativity of $R$ or $S$, or invertibility of $\varphi$ is assumed.

source.place: First sentence, exactness of scalar restriction: general finite universal-property lemma extracted by the agent. Supporting explicit internal-module (co)limit constructions: lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Mod/Limits.lean:44-244 (createsLimit and createsColimit for the forgetful functors; these are not scalar-restriction preservation declarations).

proof.text: Fix $A=R$ or $A=S$, and a finite category $J$. For any diagram $K:J\to\Mod_A(\mathcal C)$ the underlying diagram $U_AK$ has a limit and a colimit by [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]. Apply clauses 1 and 2 of [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-creates] to these cones and cocones: clause 2 applies because $A\otimes-$ preserves finite colimits, and $J$ is finite. Their lifts are respectively a limit and a colimit of $K$. Thus both module categories have finite limits and finite colimits.

source.place: First sentence; existence of finite module (co)limits, using the internal-module lifting construction, Limits.lean:109–125, 215–236.

proof.text: Put $F=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}$. By [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], $F$ gives an $S$-module $(M,\gamma_M)$ the $R$-action $\gamma_M\circ(\varphi\otimes M)$ and leaves every underlying object and morphism unchanged. Hence $U_RF=U_S$, on diagrams as well as on their cones and cocones. The linearity of the same legs after restriction is included in that definition.

source.place: First sentence; scalar restriction does not change the underlying sheaf.

proof.text: Let $K:J\to\Mod_S(\mathcal C)$ be a finite diagram. Choose a limit cone $(L,p_j)$ of $U_SK$, and lift it by clause 1 of [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-creates] to an $S$-module limit cone. Its restriction is an $R$-module cone with exactly these underlying legs. By the uniqueness of the action in clause 1 for $FK$, this is the lifted $R$-module limit cone, so it is limiting. To check preservation for any other limiting cone $c$ of $K$, take the unique cone maps between $c$ and this chosen lift. Their composites are identities by the two limit universal properties. Applying $F$ leaves these inverse identities valid, so $Fc$ is isomorphic as a cone to the limiting restricted lift. Its universal factorization is obtained by composing the latter cone's unique factorization with that isomorphism. Thus $Fc$ is limiting and $F$ preserves finite limits.

source.place: First sentence, finite-limit preservation; Limits.lean:44–115 and the restriction formula.

proof.text: For the same finite diagram $K$, choose a colimit cocone $(Q,i_j)$ of $U_SK$. Clause 2 of [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-creates] lifts it to an $S$-module colimit because $S\otimes-$ preserves these colimits. Restrict its action to $R$. The resulting cocone has underlying maps $i_j$ by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]. Since $R\otimes-$ also preserves $J$-colimits, clause 2 for $FK$ says there is a unique $R$-action making the $i_j$ linear and that this action makes the cocone colimiting. This identifies it with the restricted action, so the image of the chosen lift is colimiting. Any colimiting cocone of $K$ has mutually inverse canonical cocone maps to this lift, by uniqueness of universal factorizations. Applying $F$ preserves these inverse equations; composition with the resulting cocone isomorphism transfers the unique factorization to its image. Hence $F$ preserves every finite colimit.

source.place: First sentence, finite-colimit preservation; Limits.lean:133–221 and the restriction formula.

proof.text: Step 1 supplies the finite (co)limits required in [def-galois-exact-functor]. Steps 3 and 4 give both left and right exactness, so restriction of scalars is exact in the stated sense. The construction used only the monoidal action and preservation of finite colimits by the two left tensor functors; none of braiding, closedness, commutativity, or invertibility of $\varphi$ entered.

lean.statement: theorem finite_limits_colimits_exact_comap {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [MonoidalCategory C] [HasFiniteLimits C] [HasFiniteColimits C] {R S : C} [MonObj R] [MonObj S] (φ : R ⟶ S) [IsMonHom φ] [PreservesFiniteColimits (tensorLeft R)] [PreservesFiniteColimits (tensorLeft S)] : HasFiniteLimits (Mod C R) ∧ HasFiniteColimits (Mod C R) ∧ HasFiniteLimits (Mod C S) ∧ HasFiniteColimits (Mod C S) ∧ exactFunctor (Mod C S) (Mod C R) (comap (D := C) φ)

reviewed_lean.note: Clause-by-clause match: finite (co)limits in C, MonObj R S, IsMonHom φ (non-invertible allowed), PreservesFiniteColimits tensorLeft R and S; conclusion has the four HasFinite(Co)Limits (Mod C _) clauses plus exactFunctor (comap φ), which a probe confirmed by Iff.rfl to be PreservesFiniteLimits ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits; comap is the dependency's Mathlib match (probe: obj X = M.X by rfl). No braiding, closed, commutative, Abelian or additivity assumption; u and v independent; empty diagram covered via R⊗0≅0. Statement true: the existence clauses follow directly from the project's Mod/Limits.lean instances (probe compiled); restriction commutes with the forgetful functors that create them. Not a duplicate: the project's Mod.preservesFinite(Co)Limits_comap need Abelian and MonoidalPreadditive. Docstrings give the source place (blueprint read) and steps 1-5; sorry only; lean.statement verbatim; item node otherwise identical to live; first delivery, not dropped. nt_compile --json clean in 2.3 s with no warnings.
